On Tue, Mar 2, 2027 at 11:02 AM Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai> wrote:
> We reviewed the doc and attached a short response (RI_DPA_Response_round1.pdf) that proposes a few alternative wordings where we think mutual agreement is typical ...

Sana / MedSys team — thanks for sharing the redlines. I reviewed MedSys_DPA_Redlines_v1.docx and Tessa's response. Below are counsel-level comments (clause refs correspond to the redline file):

1) Clause 4 (Transfers & SCCs): Redwood agrees to incorporate the current EU SCCs as an addendum. We will identify roles in the Annex as Data Exporter = Redwood Inference (controller/subprocessor as applicable) and Data Importer = MedSys (controller), or vice versa depending on data flows; will clarify in Annex A. We propose language: "parties shall rely on the EU SCCs and supplement with appropriate technical & organisational measures".

2) Clause 6 (Subprocessors): Standard approach: Redwood provides a current subprocessor list and will notify 30 days prior to onboarding new critical subprocessors. We object to an open approval right; instead we propose a right to terminate for material breach tied to a subprocessor. If MedSys insists on prior approval, please specify which categories (e.g., new analytics providers, back-up storage) so we can accommodate in the Annex.

3) Clause 8 (Security & KMS): For Hosted accounts we do not yet support full BYOK for all customers. We can offer envelope encryption and customer-specific keys for Dedicated/Private plans. Recommend: insert a service-tiered KMS paragraph and allow MedSys to request an addendum for BYOK at contract execution.

4) Clause 10 (Retention & deletion): Redwood's standard is deletion of active copies within 30 days of termination with backups purged within 90 days; we can shorten backup purge to 60 days for enterprise customers with an SLA. Confirm whether MedSys requires a shorter timeline.

5) Clause 12 (Audit & Evidence): We will provide our SOC 2 Type II report under NDA and can provide specific token/usage logs for customer-scoped investigations with a standard logging export format. For recurring audit requests, propose a cost-recovery model.

6) Commands on definitions and liability cap: small editorial tweaks recommended.

Action items for Redwood (assigned):
- Provide exported subprocessor inventory (I will attach CSV).
- Attach SOC 2 link and pentest summary to the next thread message.
- Confirm KMS availability and which account tiers are eligible.

Sana — if there are specific clauses in your redline that you cannot accept (e.g., any clause that gives MedSys approval rights rather than notice), please call out clause numbers and we will propose alternative text. Also happy to jump on the call Tessa suggested — I'm free Wed 11 AM PT.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
